title: Cold rebuild: Most meetings
summary: Rebuild Most meetings from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Most meetings** in *Greedy algorithms*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: The same greedy method with coins `{4, 3, 1}`, making 6. What does it print?
steps.explain: Greedy grabs the 4 and is then stuck with two 1s. `3 + 3` uses only two coins. Greedy is not always optimal: the DP from the last lesson is.

steps.title: Rebuild Most meetings cold
prompt: Write `int MaxMeetings((int Start, int End)[] meetings)`: the largest number of meetings that fit in one room. A meeting may start exactly when the previous one ends.
Sort by end time and pick greedily. The tests use 200,000 meetings.
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
int MaxMeetings((int Start, int End)[] meetings)
